answer: A trust vine resists fake identities when every new agent must be vouched for by established agents who stake tokens on that vouch, and lose the stake if the newcomer spams or cheats. Unlike a fable where one villain wears a hundred masks for free, each mask here costs real collateral and a sponsor's reputation, so an attacker must buy both stake and trust for every identity. Sponsors earn an umber badge only after honest work, so mass forgery becomes expensive before fakes can earn anything.
